summary_oneline: Both OAuth2 examples are miswired (3LO example inherits local backends/authz and an unresolvable user 35; oauth2_server.py pages never do PKCE), exposing four latent library defects.

localization.role: builds AuthHandler(enable_authdb=False) without backends=/authz_backends=, so the local settings decide the backend list
star-imports settings.settings last, overriding AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS set by the example via os.environ.setdefault
existing pattern that pins backends and disables authz backends for an example
allow_hosts exempt branch: bearer resolution needs an existing session and never publishes request["userdata"]
loops every backend's authenticate(), catches only AuthException, accepts the first truthy result (also the method wrapper at 261)
indexes the False returned by check_token_info for a JWT without device_id -> TypeError at 154 (the 500)
always returns a truthy anonymous user + new session -> the 200 'Hello Anonymous'
binds the token to a session via self._idp.user_from_id; on failure logs the reported warning and returns {} (token issued without session claims)
takes the resource owner from the browser session cookie (check_session) and skips login/consent when a grant exists
fills profile claims from user_from_id and defaults them to "" when the lookup fails
401 'Not authenticated.' when _get_request_user_id finds neither userdata nor request.user
correct resource-server check (401 when the token has no bound session) that the decorator loop never reaches first
mock-only tests; test_unknown_user_degrades_without_raising locks the silent {} degrade
posts the code without code_verifier (no verifier is ever generated), so the token endpoint answers invalid_grant
authorize link without code_challenge for a PKCE-required public client
prints a 3LO URL with a literal <S256_hash> placeholder and no verifier
PKCE check: requires code_verifier when the code carries a challenge (correct per RFC 7636)

constraints.statement: AuthHandler already accepts backends= and authz_backends= so an application's backend list does not depend on settings.settings; its docstring names the bundled examples as the use case
constraints.implication: the example fix is wiring, not new library API

constraints.statement: Issuing a session-less token when the owner cannot be resolved is deliberate (d3f85ba: 'usable for introspection-based resource servers') and asserted by test_unknown_user_degrades_without_raising
constraints.implication: failing closed at the token endpoint is a behaviour change that must update that test and be decided explicitly

constraints.statement: is_authenticated already has explicit anonymous opt-ins (exclude list, request.allow_anonymous) covered by tests/unit/test_is_authenticated_exclude.py
constraints.implication: rejecting anonymous results in the backend loop keeps an opt-in path for apps that want anonymous access

constraints.statement: NoAuth, allow_hosts and the backend-loop semantics are used by real deployments (local settings enable 8 backends), and AuthHandler.api_login iterates backends the same way
constraints.implication: decorator/middleware changes affect every app, not only the example; they need their own tests

constraints.statement: The short HMAC key and issuer come from the developer's env/.env; the IdP binds conf.SECRET_KEY at import time
constraints.implication: the example cannot fix the key with os.environ.setdefault; at most it can warn or document

constraints.statement: APIKeyAuth also handles OAuth2 bearer JWTs (TASK-029 / af51e88 bearer branch)
constraints.implication: the fix must make APIKeyAuth decline non-API-key bearers cleanly, not stop it from reading bearers

hypotheses.statement: Both OAuth2 examples are miswired. (a) oauth2_3lo_server.py does not pin its auth configuration: the developer's settings/settings.py (8 backends incl. APIKeyAuth and NoAuth) and env/.env (allow_hosts authz, 6-byte key) override its os.environ defaults, so localhost requests take the middleware's exempt branch and fall into the decorator's backend loop, where APIKeyAuth crashes on the bearer (500) and NoAuth admits credential-less calls (200). (b) oauth2_server.py's pages never do PKCE: the token endpoint correctly demands a code_verifier, but oauth2_index.html/callback.html never generate or send one and the startup hint prints a <S256_hash> placeholder.
hypotheses.reasoning: Every link is cited: the resolved runtime config was probed, the traceback frames match decorators.py:217 and api.py:154, and the SPA sends the anonymous call with credentials:'omit', so the anonymous 200 is produced server-side. (b): the error string matches backend.py:1803 and no example page builds a PKCE pair.
hypotheses.next_probe: Pass backends=['navigator_auth.backends.oauth2.Oauth2Provider'] and authz_backends=[] to AuthHandler in the example and repeat the six clicks. For (b): run the flow from oauth2_3lo_server.py, whose page does PKCE in JS.

hypotheses.statement: user_id 35 came from a pre-existing browser session for localhost:5000 in the shared Redis store; /oauth2/authorize took that session as the resource owner without a demo login, and the demo IdP (users 1, 2) cannot resolve it, so every issued/refreshed token is session-less — producing the bind warnings, the empty userinfo and the grants 401.
hypotheses.reasoning: The session cookie is the only code path by which a non-demo user_id can reach the code; which app created that session is not provable from the code.
hypotheses.next_probe: Clear cookies for localhost:5000 (or use a private window), log in as demo/demo123 and check the token's user_id is 1.

hypotheses.statement: Independently of the example, four library defects turn a misconfiguration into wrong answers instead of a clean 401: APIKeyAuth.authenticate lacks the `if not data` guard, is_authenticated lets non-AuthException errors escape and accepts anonymous results, the allow_hosts exempt branch never publishes request["userdata"], and /oauth2/authorize + the token endpoint accept a resource owner the IdP cannot resolve.
hypotheses.reasoning: Each defect is read directly in the code; none is covered by tests and none is a recent regression (F013), so fixing the example alone would hide them again.
hypotheses.next_probe: Unit tests: APIKeyAuth.authenticate with a 3LO JWT returns None; is_authenticated with [APIKeyAuth, NoAuth] answers 401 for a bad bearer and for no credentials.

Existing 3LO tests are mock-only and do not cover the decorator loop, APIKeyAuth with an OAuth2 bearer, NoAuth or allow_hosts

no — I logged in with demo/demo123
unknowns.resolution_note: Unresolved but no longer blocking: the U3 decision (validate the session user at /oauth2/authorize, fail the token grant) covers both a foreign session cookie and any other source of an unresolvable user. Probe stays: retry in a private window with demo/demo123.

unknowns.question: Should @is_authenticated() reject anonymous results (NoAuth guest) from its backend loop, leaving the exclude list / allow_anonymous as the only ways to admit anonymous callers?
plausible_answers: yes — reject anonymous in the loop
no — keep accepting NoAuth; fix only the example

unknowns.question: When the resource owner cannot be resolved by the IdP, what should the provider do: keep issuing session-less tokens, fail the token request, or also re-validate the session user at /oauth2/authorize and force a fresh login?
plausible_answers: validate at /authorize (force login) and fail the token request
unknowns.user_answer: validate at /authorize (force login) and fail the token request

recommended_next_command.rationale: Localization is high-confidence and the fix set is bounded (example wiring + four library defects); the remaining choices are behaviour decisions answered in Q&A, not architectural forks.
